note: The court asked: why only cancer drugs?

captionHeadline: A ₹5,000 heart stent sold for over ₹25,000. Now the Supreme Court is asking questions.
summary: The Centre told the Supreme Court it has capped trade margins on anti-cancer drugs at 30% of MRP. The court asked why the cap covers only cancer drugs. The Hindu reported mark-ups of up to 1,000% on some cancer drugs, and a made-in-India cardiac stent costing about ₹5,000 sold for over ₹25,000.
forYou: Cancer medicines should get cheaper. If the court widens it, everyday medicines could follow. Always compare MRP and ask for generics.
cta: Know someone buying cancer medicines? Send them this.

summary: India's National Mental Health Survey puts the treatment gap at 83%, rising to 85.2% for major depression. captionHeadline: Is WhatsApp charging for messages now? Only if you're a big business.
summary: Meta's new India pricing applies to the WhatsApp Business Platform, which companies use to send bulk messages like order and delivery updates. forYou: Your personal chats and family groups cost nothing extra. If you run a big brand that sends bulk updates, check your bill.

captionHeadline: SBI salary account? Your free ATM visits just got cut in half.
summary: From 1 October, SBI Salary Package account holders get 5 free transactions a month at other banks' ATMs, down from 10. Balance checks count too. After the limit, each cash withdrawal costs ₹23 plus GST, and each non-cash transaction ₹11 plus GST. SBI's own ATMs are unchanged.
forYou: Use SBI ATMs where you can, and stop checking your balance at other banks' ATMs. Use the app instead.

captionHeadline: The IMF just raised India's growth forecast. The world is slowing; India isn't.
summary: The IMF's October World Economic Outlook projects India's growth at 7% in 2026 and 7% in 2027, an upgrade from its earlier forecast. It expects world growth of 3.1% in 2026 and China at 4.5%. The IMF cited "resilient domestic demand and robust services activity".
forYou: Strong growth usually means more hiring. But prices and EMIs are rising too, so watch both.

captionHeadline: Wildlife populations have crashed by an average of 73% in one lifetime.
summary: The Living Planet Index shows monitored wildlife populations have fallen by an average of 73% since 1970. Latin America and the Caribbean show a 95% average decline, Africa 80% and Europe 23%. About half of the 35,803 populations tracked are declining.
forYou: The species we grew up seeing are disappearing within a single human lifetime.

caption: Himalayan peaks are warming nearly twice as fast as the global average.
note: Ice loss in the region has doubled since 2000.
captionHeadline: The Himalayas are heating up twice as fast as the rest of the world.
summary: High mountains are warming by about 0.3°C per decade, nearly twice the global average. ICIMOD reports ice loss in the Hindu Kush Himalaya has doubled since 2000. In Nepal, a 600-metre ice-and-rock collapse sent a debris flood 170 km down the Bhote Koshi river.
forYou: Himalayan glaciers feed the Ganga, Brahmaputra and Indus. Faster melting means more floods now and less water later.

captionHeadline: By 2050, one in five Indians could be over 60. Who will care for them?
